Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-08-26 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Lark - Head of ML), Tomás Alvarez (Lark - Platform Eng), Sara Li (Lark - Product)

Optional auto-summary:
Summary: quick regression hunt on guardrails after last week's prompt changes; reviewed scorecard, identified 3 regression clusters (hallucination on invoices, redaction misses, instruction-follow failures), discussed dedicated pilot perf targets and a rollback/canary rehearsal. Agreed next steps for logs, benchmark configs, and security pack.
Topics: scorecard delta, failing prompt set, KV/prefix caching behavior, quantization vs latency tradeoff, VPC egress, SOC2 docs, canary rollback drill
Action items (brief): see metadata list

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: all right, everyone hello, uh thanks for joining on short notice. we have 46 minutes, we want to do a focused regression hunt and then ops next steps. Devon, quick status?
[00:18] Devon Park: yeah hi, uh quick recap — we pushed the prompt tightening last thursday, ran the scorecard, saw overall macro precision up 4% but three small regression clusters popped. i've got hist plots — i'll share after the call.
[00:35] Priya Rao: yep that's right, we noticed an increase in invoice hallucination and also some redaction misses where PIIs weren't scrubbed. not huge numbers but surfaced in our manual review.
[00:50] Tomás Alvarez: and from infra we saw bursty KV cache churn causing token latency spikes during replay windows, so some requests fell out of cache earlier than expected.
[01:05] Sara Li: product is worried about user-visible errors, esp around redaction. timeline: pilot needs to be stable by mid-Sept for the client demo.
[01:20] Maya Chen: understood. ok let's walk through the three clusters — Devon you got examples?
[01:30] Devon Park: yeah um i'll read a few, first cluster "invoice_total shows $0 then later says $200" — model hallucinated a line. second cluster is missing redaction where the prompt asked to redact emails but it returned them verbatim. third is instruction-follow: user asked to output JSON, but model mixed prose and JSON, which breaks our parser.
[02:05] Priya Rao: for the redaction ones, our guardrail policy is the post-processing filter plus the prompt instruction. seems like the prompt-only approach is brittle under some quantized variants.
[02:22] Tomás Alvarez: right and when we ran quant-ctx2 on the smaller GPU the redaction model path went into a fallback that dropped strict filtering. might be because of tokenization differences or kernel behavior.
[02:35] Devon Park: yeah small-quant variants sometimes change token alignments; also continuous batching increased context reuse, which can cause stale KV if the prefix caching isn't flushed correctly for user-specific redactions.
[02:55] Maya Chen: ok, so two vectors: model/config-induced behavior and runtime caching. priority which do we want to triage first?
[03:05] Priya Rao: i'd prefer model/config first — if the inference output is wrong, caching fixes won't help.
[03:12] Devon Park: agreed. i propose: (1) run the failing prompts on the non-quantized baseline to confirm regression is quant-related; (2) isolate redaction prompts in a targeted eval set; (3) run prefix flush experiment to rule out caching.
[03:32] Tomás Alvarez: can do. i can run replay over the weekend and capture TTLs and KV miss rates.
[03:40] Sara Li: will the replay require masking or can you share examples?
[03:46] Tomás Alvarez: i'll export top-failing examples but will strip PII; we can share syntheticized versions if needed.
[03:52] Maya Chen: perfect. Devon, on metrics — what are the scorecard deltas?
[03:58] Devon Park: overall precision +4, recall -1.1, safety false positive rate increased 0.3% but hallucination incidents +1.7% in the failing set. i can push the detailed chart to the g-drive link after — link: shorturl.com/redwood-lark-aug26 (placeholder).
[04:20] Priya Rao: the hallucination lift is concentrated in finance templates. do we have model-specific artifacts?
[04:28] Devon Park: yes it's concentrated when sequence length > 512 and when we use the quant-ctx2 kernel. hint: the kernel picks a different attention tiling which changes beam alignment.
[04:40] Tomás Alvarez: that matches the latency logs — at 512+ tokens we see 20-30ms extra per token on that variant.
[04:50] Maya Chen: okay technical deep-dive later, but immediate mitigation options: we can pin the hosted pilot to baseline float model for sequences >=512, or we can enable stricter post-filtering with a conservative regex/NER pipeline. pros/cons?
[05:05] Priya Rao: pinning sounds safe but costlier. we need to know cost delta.
[05:12] Maya Chen: we'll include cost delta in the pricing pack. Devon, can you estimate token cost change for pinning?
[05:18] Devon Park: rough calc: ~15% higher token cost for float at current batch rates for long sequences, but latency improves slightly and hallucination drops.
[05:27] Sara Li: is there an option to fallback only for finance templates? route by tag?
[05:33] Devon Park: yes we can route by route-tag to the float model when template detected. Redwood's routing policy supports header-based routing.
[05:40] Tomás Alvarez: that helps with cost. we can detect templates at request time, but detection must be cheap.
[05:46] Priya Rao: about redaction, can we add a locked post-processing filter that always runs in the private sidecar?
[05:52] Maya Chen: yes there is a sidecar option in Redwood Private that can do enforced post-filtering and uses your KMS for keys. note: sidecar adds ~5-10ms.
[06:02] Tomás Alvarez: 5-10ms is acceptable for our SLO.
[06:06] Devon Park: two more items — one, we noticed SAML assertions sometimes cause metadata truncation when SSO headers are long; two, audit logs currently are 48h retention in hosted pilot, you asked for 90 days in the enterprise plan.
[06:20] Priya Rao: yes we need 90-day logs and SOC2 summary for compliance review with legal. also SSO flow diagram.
[06:28] Maya Chen: we'll send the SOC2 summary and SSO flow in the security pack. included also is the RBAC examples and KMS integration notes.
[06:36] Sara Li: great. on the canary/rollback rehearsal — what does that look like?
[06:40] Devon Park: propose: stage a canary with 5% traffic -> monitor scorecard + latency for 24h -> auto-fallback to baseline float model if hallucination rate > threshold or latency breach. we can script the rollback in the Redwood Console.
[06:55] Tomás Alvarez: can we simulate the canary with replay? we'd like to do a rehearsal before live traffic.
[07:01] Devon Park: yes, run your replay to a canary endpoint in dedicated pilot; Redwood supports replaying traffic with original headers so it's a good dry-run.
[07:10] Priya Rao: timeline: we want rehearsal first week of Sept, and live canary mid-Sept.
[07:17] Maya Chen: sounds feasible. action owners noted.
[07:21] Priya Rao: quick question on quantization — could we try a hybrid: quant for short sequences and float for long?
[07:29] Devon Park: that's exactly the routing pattern i mentioned earlier. threshold-based routing is supported. we'll sample to ensure stability.
[07:36] Sara Li: ok cool. can you send the exact routing config we should apply?
[07:40] Devon Park: i'll add a config snippet to the g-drive doc.
[07:44] Maya Chen: any blockers from legal/procurement?
[07:47] Priya Rao: procurement wants the preliminary SOW and pricing to evaluate budgets. legal needs the SOC2 and data residency note.
[07:55] Maya Chen: we'll include a starter SOW and committed capacity options; send by Friday.
[07:59] Tomás Alvarez: on infra notes — i noticed a spike in egress costs when the model fell back to remote variant in another region; that's a hard cost to avoid. region pinning helps.
[08:13] Devon Park: we can pin region per-customer in Redwood Private or use routing policy to prefer local region, with fallback to global model variants.
[08:22] Priya Rao: okay. last bit: how do we track guardrail regressions over time?
[08:27] Devon Park: Redwood Console has a guardrail heatmap and timeline; we'll add a custom widget for your top-3 metrics and webhook alerts for threshold breaches.
[08:36] Sara Li: that would be helpful.
[08:39] Maya Chen: recap and next steps — i'll summarize: Redwood sends pricing/security pack + starter SOW by 2026-08-28; Devon runs baseline micro-benchmarks and posts configs by 2026-08-30; Tomás exports replay logs and top failing prompts by 2026-09-01; customer runs replay and we schedule canary rehearsal for week of 2026-09-07.
[09:02] Priya Rao: agreed. one more ask — please include an example rollback playbook.
[09:09] Maya Chen: yes we'll include a rollback playbook and a sample routing policy.
[09:13] Sara Li: thanks all.
[09:15] Tomás Alvarez: thanks, bye.
[09:17] Devon Park: bye everyone.
[09:20] Maya Chen: thanks, conference ended.

Notes: transcription contains some mis-heard technical terms (e.g., "quant-ctx2" might be a shorthand used by engineering), and some speaker labels may be approximate. References: shared doc link (placeholder) shorturl.com/redwood-lark-aug26; security pack to be attached to CRM.
